timeline.title: A Short History of Milestones
items: Ancient Rome
The first milestones
Romans set stone markers along their roads, one every Roman mile, so travellers knew how far they had come.
Ancient times
The first jubilee
In ancient Hebrew tradition, every fiftieth year was a jubilee: a time of freedom, rest and celebration.
1900 to now
More birthdays for all
Average life expectancy around the world has more than doubled, so there are more big birthdays to enjoy.
The record holder
Jeanne Calment of France died aged 122, the oldest person whose age has ever been verified.
today: Not a record breaker yet. But already a legend to everyone here.

letters.title: Wise Words on Growing Older
items: Grow old along with me! The best is yet to be.
Robert Browning, Rabbi Ben Ezra, 1864
For age is opportunity no less than youth itself, though in another dress.
Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, 1875
Old friends and old wine are best.
An old English proverb
The older the fiddle, the sweeter the tune.
An old saying
letters.hand: They knew what they were talking about. Just look at {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Getting Better
items: sun
Seasoned traveller
{age} trips around the Sun, each one about 940 million kilometres. That is a lot of air miles.
pulse
A hard working heart
Your heart beats around 35 million times a year, without ever asking for a day off.
smile
Happier with age
Many studies find people grow happier and calmer from middle age onwards. The best really is ahead.
book
A growing vocabulary
Your vocabulary can keep growing for decades, and often peaks later in life.
spark
Still learning
The brain keeps making new connections at every age. Old dogs, new tricks: confirmed.
moon
Sweet dreams
We spend roughly a third of our lives asleep, so some of your best years were spent dreaming.
facts.hand: Science agrees: {who} is not getting older, just getting better.

note.title: What we believe a milestone is
paras: We make magazines for a living, and the big birthdays are the ones we love most.
We believe a milestone is a little stone by the road that says: look how far you have come. Look at everyone who walked part of the way with you.
{who}, someone wanted to stop and mark this one properly. Not with a card anyone could buy, but with pages full of you: your stories, your face, the years that made you.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, the road ahead is full of people who adore you.
note.wish: Happy birthday, {who}. Here is to {age}, and the best is yet to be.
